pa_northwest_the.blurb: Northwest Pennsylvania spreads its climbing across gorge cliffs, forest outcrops and boulder fields instead of one hub. Bouldering makes up most of it, with top-rope and trad lines behind and only a handful of sport routes. Boulder problems run from very easy up to about V6, with the weight in the V1 to V4 range, while the roped climbs span roughly 5.4 to 5.12. McConnells Mill State Park near Portersville is the biggest sub-area and offers both bouldering and roped climbing, including a rugged section meant for experienced climbers. Beartown Rocks and Rim Rock add smaller collections, mostly boulders, and the Rimrock Trail in Allegheny National Forest is a sandstone boulder zone with something for every level.

tn_walden_s_ridge_park.blurb: Walden's Ridge Park is a forested public park on Signal Mountain's eastern side, roughly ten minutes from downtown Chattanooga. Everything here is bouldering. Problems start at V0 and run through a deep middle of V1 to V5, tapering to a few at V9. The boulders are Pennsylvanian sandstone, with a wide mix of styles. Clusters are strung along trails over the upper part of the park, including the Upper Parking Area, the Main Area boulders, Superposition Boulder and a creekside zone. Some pockets feel quiet and natural, while others sit beside trails used by hikers, bikers and runners. Many boulders have seen little traffic, so expect some loose rock on the climbs and in the landing zones, and bring pads.

va_picnic_area.blurb: This part of Grayson Highlands State Park in southwest Virginia is all bouldering. Problems begin at V0 and build through a deep middle of V2 to V6, with a fair number of harder lines reaching into double digits. The Picnic Area Boulders are tucked among old rhododendron close to the trails, and they feature steep, overhanging lines on big blocks. Beyond them sit the Upchurch, Outlaw and Spring Ridge groups. Around the park the stone has a sharp texture that gives plenty of friction but can be rough on skin, and many boulders stand in open, windswept meadows. Conditions are generally workable from late March into early November, with snow possible outside that stretch.

bc_terrace.blurb: Terrace lies in northwest British Columbia along Highway 16 and is built around granite, from big multi-pitch walls to smaller single-pitch crags with short approaches. Trad and sport routes are roughly even, with a solid bouldering scene beside them and a few ice and mixed lines. Most roped climbs fall between 5.8 and 5.12, bunching around 5.10, and boulder problems stay mostly in the V0 to V4 range. Copper Mountain is the main draw, with long pitches finished at bolted stations, while Kitselas offers four close-together south-facing walls of approachable single-pitch routes that suit beginners and groups. Terrace Mountain, Exstew and Exchamsiks fill out the choices. Late spring through early fall is the comfortable window; outside it conditions turn crisp.

ca_pine_mountain.blurb: Pine Mountain is a sandstone boulder field strung along a forested ridgeline in Los Padres National Forest, north of Ojai at roughly 7,000 feet. It is almost purely bouldering, with problems on both the north and south slopes. Grades run from V0 up to V11, with the largest group at V0 and a steady supply from V1 through V5. Many problems are highball, the rock is mostly solid, and the style rewards sustained technique over raw power, so bring several pads and spotters. Happy Hunting Grounds, the Picnic Area Boulders and Enlightenment Ridge hold most of the problems, and the Picnic Area suits newer climbers and families. Late spring through early fall gives the best weather, and snow can close the season in winter.

co_montrose.blurb: Montrose, in western Colorado, offers sandstone bouldering and sport climbing within easy reach of town. Bouldering is the larger share, mostly V0 to V3 with a smaller set of harder problems, and sport routes follow, mainly 5.10 to 5.11 with a spread of easier lines. Electric Hills holds scattered boulders across three drainages on highly featured sandstone that is grittier and softer than Dry Creek, with plenty of fun easier climbing and room for new problems. Dry Creek is a west-facing sandstone cliff of 30 to 50 feet, shaded until about noon, with incut holds and mostly bolted lines. Expect hot, dry, breezy days, tiny gnats in spring, and soft rock after rain or snow.
